rationale: M60.P1 (#873) — a relationship row must carry ONE line base. Eight writers in the typescript analyzer stored `startPosition.row` (0-based) in `metadata.line` while the same row's `line_number` is 1-based (as is every line in every other analyzer's payload), so the mirror disagreed with its own row; where the mirror's node also differed from the `lineField` node the disagreement was larger than one. Measured through the PRODUCTION pipeline before the fix (script/m59/probe-metadata-line-base.ts, four real corpus files per language from grails-core, scala3, lodash, element-plus and nlohmann-json): typescript 155 of 198 rows carry both fields and 148 were off by one with 7 off by more; tsx 179 of 231 with 173 off by one and 6 by more; vue 3 of 18 with 3 off by one; and ZERO rows on java (813 relationships), scala (1,958), groovy (81), gradle (566), cpp (1,069), hpp (1,852), python (440), js (8) or swift (2) — only this analyzer writes the mirror, so the defect was never a JVM one. AFTER the fix the same sweep reports 337 of 337 rows agreeing, 0 off by one, 0 off by more. The fix is two-part on purpose: the eight writers now stamp the 1-based site (and the `new`-expression site now uses the SAME node `lineField` stamps, which is what the larger disagreements were), and a single normalisation pass makes the two fields agree by construction so a ninth writer cannot reintroduce a second base; the pass only ever corrects a number that is present — absence stays absence, which is the ruled 'unknown is a first-class state' contract (voiced by the two `exports` rows below, which carry no metadata.line at all and are expected to keep carrying none). The one internal reader of the mirror — `filterPhantomDupKeyEdges`, which tests whether an edge's site lies inside a collapsed duplicate-key member's dead span — moved with the base (`startRow + 1` / `endRow + 1`); comparing a 1-based site against 0-based bounds would have widened the dead span by a line at each end, which is why the base change could not be done in the writer alone.
